items.body: أكد لويس دي لا فوينتي، المدير الفني لمنتخب إسبانيا، ثقته الكبيرة في قدرات فريقه قبل المواجهة المرتقبة أمام فرنسا في ربع نهائي دوري الأمم الأوروبية، بعدما أوقعت القرعة المنتخبين في مواجهة قوية يومي 25 و28 مارس المقبل. وتحدث المدرب الإسباني عن اللقاء المنتظر، مشيرًا إلى أن مواجهة فرنسا ستكون اختبارًا صعبًا أمام أحد أقوى المنتخبات على مستوى العالم، لكنه شدد في الوقت نفسه على أن منتخب بلاده يمتلك الأفضلية، معتبرًا أن إسبانيا هي المنتخب الأفضل في العالم حاليًا. وقال دي لا فوينتي في تصريحات نقلتها شبكة " فوت ميركاتو " الفرنسية: "نتطلع بشوق كبير لهذه المباراة أمام فرنسا، ومن الواضح أن أمامنا وقتًا كافيًا للاستعداد ودراسة الاستراتيجية المناسبة بعناية، لكن الأهم أن هناك شيئًا ترسخ في أذهاننا منذ مباراة كأس العالم". ولعب المنتخبان الإسباني والفرنسي في نصف نهائي كأس العالم 2026 ، وفازت كتيبة الماتادور (2-0)، قبل أن تحقق اللقب العالمي على حساب الأرجنتين في المباراة النهائية (1-0). وأضاف المدرب الإسباني أن الجهاز الفني سبق أن استخدم رسالة تحفيزية قبل مواجهة المنتخبين في كأس العالم، مؤكدًا أنه سيعتمد عليها مجددًا خلال التحضير للمباراتين المقبلتين. وأوضح: "استعددنا لتلك المباراة برسالة سنستخدمها بالتأكيد مرة أخرى، سنواجه فريقًا قويًا للغاية، أحد أفضل الفرق في العالم بلا شك، لكنهم سيواجهون أفضل ف…

items.title: Penguin shows off photonic memory box at SC26 that can expand AI accelerator capacity over optical links
items.summary: Penguin Solutions demonstrates external memory box with up to 576 GB of HBM3E and 16 TB of DDR5 inside that connects to hosts using optical links. There is a major caveat with this one as it does not seem to support existing servers and accelerators.
items.body: Penguin Solutions showed off its MemoryAI Photonic Appliance remote memory system at Supercomputer 2026 ( SC26 ), with customer samples scheduled for the second half of 2027. The device supports up to 576 GB of HBM3E with an aggregate bandwidth of up to 7.2 TB/s, and connects to systems using optical interconnects via the CXL.mem 3.1 protocol. HBM memory capacity is usually one of the major bottlenecks of contemporary AI accelerators, which is why, when developers face it, they tend to add or upgrade their accelerators. Penguin Solutions' new device aims to solve that, but there are drawbacks. The MemoryAI Photonic Appliance is designed to accommodate up to 576 GB of HBM3E and 16 TB of DDR5 memory, with overall bandwidth targeting 7.2 TB/s. The external memory box supports three memory access configurations: HBM Direct Mode, HBM-DDR5 Cached Mode, and DDR5 Direct Mode. The first provides access to external HBM3E, the second combines HBM3E and DDR5 in a tiered memory sub-system with HBM3E acting like a write-through cache for DDR5, while the third provides access to DDR5 without an intermediate HBM cache. The 3D printer accessory company’s first 3D printer aims to bring IQEX technology to the masses at a budget price, with an SRP of only $899. It has already raised over $500,000, crushing its goal of only $9,820. Independent Quad Extrusion, or IQEX, is unlike tool-changer 3D printers. Instead of one print head swapping assemblies, it has four individual print heads. This allows for increased productivity by printing with all four heads at once, or reducing waste by not going through any purging steps. The Co Print Quadro is a non-enclosed bedslinger, and its design is quite similar to the Bambu Lab A1 , albeit much beefier. items.title: The RTX 5090’s 16-pin connector just got a free pin-by-pin watchdog
items.summary: RTX Lens, a free open-source Windows app, reads per-pin current from Asus ROG Astral GPUs, WireView Pro II and MSI PSUs.
items.body: A developer known as Codeh4ck released a free, open-source Windows app , RTX Lens, to help assuage melting power connector fears for owners of powerful RTX 5080 and 5090 GPUs. The app can read per-pin current information on Asus Astral cards, the WireView Pro II GPU monitoring device from Thermal Grizzly, and MSI MPG Ai1300TS/Ai1600TS PSUs, enabling an optional shutdown for persistent warnings. It works by reading current at the GPU, PSU, or both ends of the cable, and can even notify you by phone to provide extra protection for your investment. The project’s README says that the app allows reading of “GPU power, pin currents, and temperatures at a glance.” The per-pin monitoring is the important part here, as the 12V-2x6 connection carries current on six 12V pins with a rating of about 9A, with Asus’s warning at 9.2A, and exceeding the per-pin limit has led to melted connectors . An RTX 5090 is rated at 575W of board power, which is close to the connector’s 600W rating. This led to the app’s construction, the developer says, due to “double paranoia about the 12VHPWR connector melting, since I own 2 5090s.” (Image credit: RTX Lens ) For supported Asus ROG Astral RTX 5080 and 5090 …

items.title: AI agents design an entirely new CPU architecture from scratch, startup claims
items.summary: Architect Labs says its AI agents designed Frostbite, an interaction-net CPU with 4.59x the performance per watt of an in-order core.
items.body: Architect Labs, a Palo Alto startup, said in a research blog post that its AI systems discovered, designed, and verified Frostbite, a general-purpose CPU with a new instruction set “built from the ground up.” Across 25 workloads, a four-tile Frostbite cluster delivered 4.59 times the performance per watt of a similarly sized “silicon-proven” dual-issue, in-order CPU core. Those numbers come from a simulated 7nm design that has not yet been made in silicon, and the company says it can’t name the comparison core for legal reasons. Conventional CPUs have hardware that “rediscovers, at runtime, which instructions actually depend on each other.” Multicore designs also need deep cache hierarchies and coherence protocols, which keep every core’s view of shared memory consistent, but scale poorly and cost area and power. Architect Labs’ alternative is what it calls “multithreading for free,” where the program itself exposes the parallel work, without threads, locks, or out-of-order hardware required for that discovery. items.title: Moore Threads' next 'Lushan' gaming GPU could pack a record 64GB of VRAM
items.summary: Moore Threads teased its Lushan gaming GPU ahead of MDC 2026, with a product manager claiming record VRAM for a consumer graphics card.
items.body: Moore Threads’ MTT S80 product manager says that the next Lushan gaming GPU will have more VRAM than any consumer graphics card currently available, VideoCardz reports. With Nvidia’s RTX 5090 already at 32GB, Lushan would need more than that. This matches the previous promise of four times the company’s MTT S80’s 16GB, putting the flagship Lushan at 64GB. Moore Threads apparently hasn’t given up on graphics, even four years after the MTT S80’s release. The company teased the card earlier this week with a poster for MDC 2026, its developer conference, showing a graphics card under a black cloth on a mountainside, and put Lushan’s name in the title of the post. It has previously indicated that Lushan products would arrive before the end of the year. Although nothing the product manager stated is an official statement, his words suggest that the new Lushan GPU could feature the largest memory capacity yet offered on a consumer graphics card, which certainly draws a lot of attention from gamers and local AI enthusiasts alike. items.title: Lenders back SpaceX's $43 billion Nvidia GPU deal but worry the collateral could end up in orbit, making them impossible to reclaim if Musk defaults
items.summary: The $43 billion loan is structured as a unique arrangement in which a different company buys the Nvidia chips, while SpaceX makes quarterly payments to use them.
items.body: Elon Musk is borrowing $43 billion to finance SpaceX's acquisition of Nvidia AI chips for its ambitious data center projects and is using the semiconductors as collateral. However, Ars Technica reports that lenders are concerned that SpaceX will use the chips for its planned orbital data center , making it difficult, if not impossible, for creditors to reclaim in case the company defaults on its loan. SpaceX said it will deploy the collateralized chips only on Earth, but it remains unclear whether this provision is included in the signed debt instrument. SpaceX is working on building massive data centers on both Earth and in space. Musk has already revealed the company’s first-generation AI1 satellite , with a 120-kilowatt payload and a span that’s larger than a Boeing 747, while he’s also planning to build a $24-billion gas-powered AI supercomputer in Starbase, Texas. items.title: Energy companies deploy drones that can be recharged by straddling power lines
items.summary: NOMADs are drones that can land on live high-voltage lines, charge from the line itself and relocate ready for their next task.
items.body: Tech startup Nomadic showcased its NOMAD drones this week alongside an announcement that it had raised $6 million in seed funding. These quadcopter drones have a unique skill hinted at by their name: they can basically fly forever without returning to base. NOMADs recharge by perching on high-voltage power lines, a ubiquitous feature of most landscapes, before moving on to their next task. We hadn’t heard anything about the NOMAD drones until now, but Nomadic says it has tested its quadcopters for over 20,000 hours on live lines in Germany, Norway, and the U.S. “NOMADs are drones that land on live high-voltage lines, charge from the line itself, and relocate across the grid to where measurements are needed,” summarizes the startup. The reference to measurements along the power grid reveals the current purpose of NOMAD drones. They are deployed to monitor the high-voltage lines from which they leech their energy. This is a very useful task for power companies. Nomadic explains that while modern grid operators use weather models to decide how much power each line can carry, the qualities of the lines can be quite variable. items.title: Dev squeezes an AI language model onto a floppy for 486DX and Pentium PC stalwarts
items.summary: An inspired developer has shoehorned a language model onto a floppy disk created especially for 486DX and Pentium PC users running DOS.
items.body: An inspired developer has shoehorned a language model onto a floppy disk created especially for 486DX and Pentium PC users running DOS. Please note that WollyMonjac’s project isn’t a large language model (LLM). Though it shares the transformer model architecture of its much bigger siblings, Tiny 2.1 is humbly described as “a tiny question-answering transformer written in Turbo C 2.0.” (Image credit: WollyMonjac ) There isn’t much room for modern software on a floppy disk, with a typical PC formatted disk in the 486 era boasting just shy of 1,475,000 bytes of data capacity. Tiny 2.1 makes the best use of this limited headroom as possible, fitting in the following: 367,000 parameters: 4 layers, 96 wide, reads and writes letter by letter 8-bit weights (one scale per row), 380 KB in all Trained on about 3,500 facts, each asked in many wordings Your creaky old PC will need about 540KB of free conventional memory to run Tiny 2.1. If you do test it, we are sure you will appreciate the clean UI with its conversation history pane, neural monitor panel, and Ask Tiny prompt window.
